SHOPPING CENTER LEASE
(Triple Net)
ASPEN GROVE MARKETPLACE
This Shopping Center Lease ("Lease") is made as of December 10, 2020 (the "Lease Date") between
MERIDIAN RETAIL PROPERTIES, LLC, a Colorado limited liability company ("Landlord"), and
BLUEBIRD COFFEE & BAKERY, LLC, a Colorado limited liability company ("Tenant").
ARTICLE 1 - BASIC LEASE PROVISIONS
1.1 Center Aspen Grove Marketplace, 12500 E. Sample Parkway, Centennial, Colorado 80112
(the "Center"), consisting of Buildings A, B and C.
1.2 Premises Suite 140, Building B, containing approximately 7,500 rentable square feet ("RSF").
1.3 Center GLA 62,500 RSF, being the total leasable area of all buildings in the Center ("Center GLA").
1.4 Pro Rata Share 12.00% (Premises RSF of 7,500 divided by Center GLA of 62,500), as further provided
in Section 4.9.
1.5 Term Ten (10) years, commencing March 1, 2021 ("Commencement Date") and expiring
February 28, 2031.
1.6 Base Rent Years 1: $24.00 per RSF per year ($180,000.00 annually; $15,000.00 monthly),
increasing 3.0% on each anniversary of the Commencement Date.
1.7 Estimated Operating
Expense Payments
Initially $4,200.00 per month, subject to adjustment under Section 4.10.
1.8 Security Deposit $30,000.00.
1.9 Permitted Use Operation of a coffee shop, cafe and bakery with ancillary retail sales, and for no other
purpose.
1.10 Notice Addresses Landlord: Meridian Retail Properties, LLC, Attn: Property Management, 800 Example
Plaza, Suite 400, Denver, CO 80202. Tenant: at the Premises.
ARTICLE 2 - PREMISES AND TERM
2.1 Demise. Landlord leases to Tenant, and Tenant leases from Landlord, the Premises for the Term, together
with the non-exclusive right to use the Common Areas of the Center in common with other tenants, subject to the
Rules and Regulations.
2.2 Common Areas. "Common Areas" means all parking areas, driveways, sidewalks, landscaped areas, lighting,
signage structures, trash enclosures and other areas of the Center designated by Landlord for the general use of
tenants and their customers.
2.3 Delivery. Tenant accepts the Premises in its "as-is" condition, subject to Landlord's work described in Exhibit
A.
ARTICLE 3 - RENT
3.1 Base Rent. Tenant shall pay Base Rent in equal monthly installments in advance on the first day of each
calendar month, without notice, demand, deduction or offset except as expressly provided in this Lease.
3.2 Additional Rent. All sums payable by Tenant under this Lease other than Base Rent, including Operating
Expenses under Article 4, are "Additional Rent."

ARTICLE 4 - OPERATING EXPENSES (CAM, TAXES AND INSURANCE)
4.1 Tenant's Obligation. In addition to Base Rent, Tenant shall pay Tenant's Pro Rata Share of (a) CAM
Expenses, (b) Taxes, and (c) Insurance Costs (collectively, "Operating Expenses"), plus the Administrative Fee
described in Section 4.5.
4.2 CAM Expenses. "CAM Expenses" means the reasonable and actual costs paid by Landlord to operate,
maintain and repair the Common Areas, limited to: landscaping; parking lot sweeping, striping and minor repair;
snow and ice removal; Common Area utilities; Common Area lighting maintenance; security patrol; trash
removal; janitorial service for Common Areas; general repairs and maintenance of the Common Areas; and wages
and benefits of the on-site property manager and on-site maintenance personnel, prorated for time devoted to the
Center.
4.3 Exclusions from CAM Expenses. CAM Expenses shall not include: (a) capital expenditures, except as
expressly permitted by Section 4.4; (b) depreciation, mortgage principal or interest, ground rent or other costs of
financing; (c) leasing commissions, advertising, and legal, accounting or other fees incurred in negotiating,
enforcing or litigating any lease, including this Lease and the leases of other tenants; (d) salaries, wages, bonuses
or benefits of any personnel above the level of on-site property manager, including regional, executive or asset
management personnel; (e) costs reimbursed or reimbursable by insurance, warranties, condemnation awards or
other tenants; (f) fines, penalties, late charges and interest; (g) costs of correcting defects in original construction;
(h) costs of operating any property other than the Center, unless fairly allocated on a documented basis; (i)
Landlord's general corporate overhead; and (j) any cost or expense billed more than once, whether in the same or
in different calendar years.
4.4 Capital Expenditures. Capital expenditures may be included in CAM Expenses only if (i) the improvement
is reasonably intended to reduce Operating Expenses, or (ii) it is required by laws first enacted after the
Commencement Date. Any such cost shall be amortized on a straight-line basis over its useful life (not to exceed
ten (10) years for lighting and electrical improvements and twenty (20) years for all other improvements), without
interest, and only the amortized portion attributable to the applicable calendar year may be included in Operating
Expenses for that year. Replacement of the roof, roof membrane, structural elements or foundations, and
replacement (as opposed to repair) of paving, are Landlord's sole cost and shall not be included in Operating
Expenses in any amount.
4.5 Administrative Fee. Landlord may charge an administrative fee equal to twelve percent (12%) of CAM
Expenses actually billed to Tenant for the calendar year, excluding from the fee base all Taxes, all Insurance
Costs, Common Area utilities, amortized capital costs under Section 4.4, and the Administrative Fee itself (the
"Administrative Fee"). The Administrative Fee is in lieu of, and not in addition to, any other management,
supervisory or overhead charge.
4.6 Limitation on Controllable CAM Expenses. Beginning with calendar year 2022, Controllable CAM
Expenses billed for any calendar year shall not exceed one hundred six percent (106%) of Controllable CAM
Expenses billed for the immediately preceding calendar year (non-cumulative and non-compounding).
"Controllable CAM Expenses" means all CAM Expenses other than Taxes, Insurance Costs, snow and ice
removal, Common Area utilities, and amortized capital costs permitted by Section 4.4. The limitation applies to
the total Center-wide amount before application of Tenant's Pro Rata Share.
4.7 Taxes. "Taxes" means real property taxes and installments of assessments levied against the Center and
payable during the calendar year. Taxes exclude (a) income, franchise, gift, estate and inheritance taxes; (b)
penalties and interest; and (c) any increase in Taxes, and any special or supplemental assessment, attributable to a
sale, transfer, refinancing or other change in ownership or financing of the Center.
4.8 Insurance Costs. "Insurance Costs" means premiums for commercial property (all-risk) insurance and
commercial general liability insurance covering the Center, in amounts customary for comparable shopping
centers in the Denver metropolitan area. Insurance Costs exclude premiums for (a) umbrella or excess liability

coverage exceeding $5,000,000 per occurrence; (b) policies carried at the corporate or portfolio level of Landlord
or its affiliates, including directors and officers, errors and omissions, and crime coverage; and (c) deductibles or
self-insured retentions in excess of $10,000 per occurrence.
4.9 Tenant's Pro Rata Share. Tenant's Pro Rata Share is a fraction, the numerator of which is the RSF of the
Premises and the denominator of which is the Center GLA, whether or not any space in the Center is occupied or
leased. Tenant's Pro Rata Share is 12.00% as of the Lease Date and shall not be increased by reason of vacancy or
non-payment by other tenants. It shall be adjusted only upon a physical expansion or reduction of the Center
GLA, and then only upon written notice from Landlord stating the new Center GLA.
4.10 Estimated Payments. Tenant shall pay, together with each monthly installment of Base Rent, one-twelfth of
Landlord's reasonable estimate of Tenant's annual Operating Expenses. Landlord may revise the estimate not
more than once per calendar year upon thirty (30) days' written notice.
4.11 Annual Reconciliation. Within one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of each calendar year, Landlord
shall deliver to Tenant a statement (the "Reconciliation Statement") showing in reasonable detail, by line item, the
Operating Expenses for the year, the calculation of Tenant's Pro Rata Share, and the estimated payments received
from Tenant. Any shortfall shall be due thirty (30) days after Tenant's receipt of the Reconciliation Statement; any
overpayment shall be credited against the next amounts due or, if the Term has ended, refunded within thirty (30)
days. Landlord's late delivery of a Reconciliation Statement does not waive Landlord's right to a shortfall, but no
interest or late charge shall accrue on any shortfall before the thirtieth (30th) day after Tenant's receipt of the
Reconciliation Statement.
4.12 Tenant's Audit Rights. Within ninety (90) days after receipt of a Reconciliation Statement (the "Review
Period"), Tenant may give written notice objecting to the statement and requesting to inspect Landlord's books
and records, including invoices, allocation schedules and occupancy records, supporting the statement. Landlord
shall make the records available within thirty (30) days after the request. If Tenant does not object within the
Review Period, the Reconciliation Statement shall be binding on Tenant as to that year. Landlord shall refund any
overcharge within thirty (30) days after it is determined, and if the overcharge exceeds three percent (3%) of the
amount properly chargeable, Landlord shall also reimburse Tenant's reasonable audit costs.
ARTICLE 5 - USE; COMPLIANCE
5.1 Use. Tenant shall use the Premises only for the Permitted Use and shall comply with all applicable laws,
health codes and the Rules and Regulations.
5.2 Hours; Trade Name. Tenant shall open for business no later than ninety (90) days after the Commencement
Date and shall operate under the trade name "Bluebird Coffee & Bakery."
ARTICLE 6 - MAINTENANCE AND REPAIRS
6.1 Landlord. Landlord shall maintain, repair and replace, at its cost except as provided in Article 4, the roof,
structural elements, foundation and exterior walls of Building B and the Common Areas.
6.2 Tenant. Tenant shall maintain the interior of the Premises, including the heating, ventilation and air
conditioning equipment serving the Premises, plumbing fixtures, storefront glass and interior finishes, in good
order and repair.
ARTICLE 7 - INSURANCE; INDEMNITY
7.1 Tenant's Insurance. Tenant shall carry commercial general liability insurance of not less than $1,000,000 per
occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate, and property insurance on its improvements and personal property, naming
Landlord as an additional insured.
7.2 Indemnity. Each party shall indemnify the other against claims arising from its negligence or willful
misconduct. Each waives subrogation to the extent of insurance proceeds.

ARTICLE 8 - ALTERATIONS; ASSIGNMENT
8.1 Alterations. Tenant shall not make structural alterations without Landlord's prior written consent, not to be
unreasonably withheld.
8.2 Assignment. Tenant shall not assign this Lease or sublet the Premises without Landlord's prior written
consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed.
ARTICLE 9 - DEFAULT; REMEDIES
9.1 Default. Tenant is in default if it fails to pay Rent within five (5) days after written notice, or fails to perform
any other obligation within thirty (30) days after written notice.
9.2 Remedies. Upon default Landlord may terminate this Lease or Tenant's right to possession and pursue all
remedies available at law, subject to Landlord's duty to mitigate damages as required by Colorado law.
ARTICLE 10 - GENERAL
10.1 Governing Law. This Lease is governed by the laws of the State of Colorado.
10.2 Entire Agreement. This Lease, with its Exhibits, is the entire agreement of the parties and may be amended
only by a writing signed by both parties.
10.3 Notices. Notices shall be in writing and delivered by hand, nationally recognized overnight courier or
certified mail to the addresses in Section 1.10.

FIRST AMENDMENT TO SHOPPING CENTER LEASE
This First Amendment ("Amendment") is made as of October 15, 2023 and is effective as of January 1, 2024
(the "Amendment Effective Date"), between MERIDIAN RETAIL PROPERTIES, LLC ("Landlord") and
BLUEBIRD COFFEE & BAKERY, LLC ("Tenant"), and amends the Shopping Center Lease dated December
10, 2020 (the "Lease") for Suite 140 at Aspen Grove Marketplace.
1. Consideration. In consideration of Tenant's agreement to extend its operating hours to include Sunday service
and to relocate its pylon sign panel to the upper position, and other good and valuable consideration, the parties
agree as follows.
2. Administrative Fee. Section 4.5 of the Lease is amended by deleting "twelve percent (12%)" and substituting
"ten percent (10%)" for all calendar years beginning with calendar year 2024. All exclusions from the fee base in
Section 4.5 remain in effect.
3. Limitation on Controllable CAM Expenses. Section 4.6 of the Lease is amended by deleting "one hundred
six percent (106%)" and substituting "one hundred five percent (105%)" for all calendar years beginning with
calendar year 2024. The limitation remains non-cumulative and non-compounding.
4. Pro Rata Share. Landlord and Tenant confirm that the Center GLA is 62,500 RSF, that there has been no
expansion or reduction of the Center GLA since the Lease Date, and that Tenant's Pro Rata Share remains
12.00%.
5. Ratification. Except as expressly amended hereby, all terms of the Lease remain unmodified and in full force
and effect. In the event of a conflict between this Amendment and the Lease, this Amendment controls.
